findings.title: Constructor reserve mapping and duplicate-before-allocation order lack discriminating controls
findings.evidence: D5/P3 specify QueryOverlay::new and FeedRegistry::new cardinality->duplicates->checked allocations and CapacityExceeded for checked-size/reserve refusal. A01/Task2 list only affected-copy,claim-stage,fact-append,snapshot-row and per-row-reason sites;Task3 adds no constructor reserve/order fault rows.
findings.counterexample: A constructor that reserves before duplicate preflight,or panics/maps ArithmeticOverflow on reserve refusal,can satisfy all currently named constructor success/duplicate tests when ordinary small allocations succeed;existing A01 injections never reach these constructors.
minimal_repair: Extend existing CP06-A01 and Task2/Task3 with QueryOverlay owned-copy and both FeedRegistry required/received allocation branches;keep25 IDs and all original subsets.

For each branch inject the already allowed owner-local cfg(test) deterministic TryReserveError through its normal mapping;require CapacityExceeded,no normally returned owner,unchanged borrowed input and restored unique positive.

With reserve faults armed,overlength and within-limit duplicate declarations must return the ruled length error or DuplicateKey without hitting a reserve site;add a valid unique admitted declaration per site to prove the injection is reachable.
Use an unsorted unique required[1,0] positive to verify the frozen sorted-ID/received-bit association;mutate ordering/error mapping to require the intended assertion failure.
